exercise.name: Iso-Lateral Low Row
library_steps: Sit with your chest on the pad and grip the low handles.
Pull the handles back toward your hips, elbows close.
Let them go forward slowly until your arms are straight.
exercise.one_line_summary: Seated with the chest on a pad, neutral handles low in front. Picture 1: arms reaching forward and down; picture 2: elbows pulled back close to the body, hands by the hips.

movement.end: 35 deg, elbows back past the hips

muscles.emg: Low pull back to the hips = shoulder extension with the arms close, a strong latissimus action (S1, S3).
muscles.surface: Side and lower back, under the armpit.

muscles.role: Low demand with the chest supported (S2).

mistakes.why_it_matters: Keep the pull in the back (S1).

sources.citation: Lehman GJ, Buchan DD, Lundy A, Myers N, Nalborczyk A. Variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises: an experimental study. Dyn Med. 2004;3(1):4.
sources.what_it_gave: Seated row gave the highest middle trapezius/rhomboid activity; wide-grip pulldown and seated row had the best lat-to-biceps ratio.

sources.citation: Fenwick CM, Brown SH, McGill SM. Comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load, and stiffness. J Strength Cond Res. 2009;23(5):1408-1417.
sources.what_it_gave: Rowing variants compared: latissimus dorsi, trapezius, erector spinae activity; supported rows reduce lumbar load.

sources.citation: Padovan R, Ce E, Longo S, Tornatore G, Esposito F, Coratella G. High-density surface electromyography excitation of prime movers across scapular positions in the seated row. J Funct Morphol Kinesiol. 2025;11(1):6.
sources.what_it_gave: Seated row HD-EMG: latissimus, trapezius and posterior deltoid excitation across shoulder-blade positions.

clip_check.target: 68 deg, forward and down -> 35 deg, elbows back past the hips (within 10 deg)

clip_check.check: Machine parts meet the hands/feet; levers keep their length
clip_check.target: moving rod lengths equal at start and end (+-1 cm)
